mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.5% signals accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates and increases liquidity, directly boosting equity valuations and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of the 20-day windows following months with FEDFUNDS <= 0.5% over a 5-year walk-forward period.

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 5.5% indicates deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following months with UNRATE > 5.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5.5% and year-over-year CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 1.5% signals stagflationary risk that reduces corporate profit margins and triggers equity market sell-offs, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following months with UNRATE > 5.5% and CPIAUCSL_YoY < 1.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 600 thousand units per month during late-cycle expansions indicates robust consumer demand for residential construction, which supports corporate revenue growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following months with HOUST > 600 during late-cycle expansions.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production (INDPRO) falling below 100 (index 2017=100) indicates manufacturing contraction that reduces corporate output and profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following months with INDPRO < 100.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles, a federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) rise above 0.5% signals reduced liquidity and higher borrowing costs that depress equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following months with FEDFUNDS > 0.5% during monetary tightening cycles.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly GDP growth rate (GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates robust economic expansion that supports corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the 60-day windows following quarters with GDPC1 growth > 2%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous industrial production (INDPRO) decline below 100 and federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) increase above 0.5% signals a contractionary economic cycle that reduces corporate investment and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 40% of the 5-day windows following months with INDPRO < 100 and FEDFUNDS > 0.5%.
